title: Tokyo and Kyoto, nine days
subtitle: A fictional sample trip used by the skill
headline: Tokyo and Kyoto, nine days
lede: A fictional eight-night trip used as a sample for this skill. Places, flights, hotels and booking notes are invented. It shows Japan-typical patterns: restaurant reservations through TableCheck, Tabelog and Omakase, a walk-in ramen shop, a Shinkansen transfer, an IC-card note, and an attraction with timed tickets.
dietary_note: Nora is vegetarian. Sam has no restrictions. diet_fit is judged against the union (vegetarian).
overview_notes: Both cities and the transfer between them are booked. Restaurant and ticket reservations still open are on the tasks list.
nights_chart_caption: Four booked nights in Tokyo, then four booked nights in Kyoto.
status_legend: Booked — flights, both stays, and the Shinkansen are confirmed.
Open — still to decide or book (a recommended lunch and a timed-ticket pavilion).

budget_plan.notes: Flights, hotels and the Shinkansen are already paid; remainder is food, local transit and tickets.

pace.notes: Four nights in Tokyo, then four in Kyoto. No day trips that need a third hotel.

transport.notes: Trains and an IC card (Suica, Pasmo or ICOCA) for local transit. No rental car.

already_booked_notes: Outbound and return flights, both stays, and the Tokyo–Kyoto Shinkansen are booked. Confirmations can be dropped into inbox/.

entry_checks.visa: For this sample party (US passports, short tourism stay in Japan): visa exemption is typical for stays under 90 days, but confirm on official US and Japanese government pages, and complete any current pre-arrival process (for example Visit Japan Web) before travel. This note is illustrative.
entry_checks.passport_validity: Japan often expects a passport valid for the duration of the stay. Re-check the current rule. Sample only.
entry_checks.insurance: Not a legal entry requirement for this sample route, but travel medical insurance is strongly recommended. Confirm card-packaged cover and whether a top-up is needed.
entry_checks.power_adapters: Japan uses Type A and Type B sockets, 100 V / 50 or 60 Hz (Tokyo is 50 Hz). A Type A adapter is enough for typical US dual-voltage chargers. A short conversion plug is usually all that is needed.

problem_dates.note: Children's Day, at the end of Golden Week (sample year). This trip starts after that holiday week, so crowds should have eased; re-check local calendars.

entry_checks.notes: Illustrative research for a fictional sample trip. Always re-check official sources.
